# Composable Sensory Rules and Conditional Tile Artwork

> **For agentic workers:** Execute the approved side-conversation design in dependency order using superpowers:executing-plans and TDD. Manual player acceptance belongs to the user; never block this work on player logins, browser automation, or unlocking the Mac.

**Goal:** Compose independent emission, glow perception and hearing Rule Elements on ordinary Effects, and separately gate native tile artwork by a selected owned PC's Effect rank.

**Architecture:** Register native PF2e/SF2e RuleElement subclasses with autogenerated native Rules-tab forms. Resolve shared canonical world rules against each application, keeping native counters individual. Tiles consume emission rules; Ambient Sounds broadcast an explicit channel. Artwork eligibility changes only native mesh artwork opacity, leaving visibility, depth restrictions, walls, fog, floors and clipping intact.

**Tech stack:** Existing TypeScript, Foundry v14, SF2e/PF2e native RuleElement API, Vitest. No dependency additions.

**Spec:** User-approved side-task handoff 2026-09-25, replacing the single-channel Details fieldset in the [original design](../specs/2026-09-25-sensory-effects-design.md).

## Binding decisions

- Independent Emit, Perceive and Hear rules support several channels and ordinary rules on one Effect. No campaign names, colours, distances or thresholds in feature code.
- Actor and tile ranks remain individual; world rule edits remain shared. Preserve native Unidentified and GM-only template ownership.
- Only selected owned tokens supply sensory viewpoints. Tile artwork specifically requires a selected owned character; ANY qualifying selection satisfies it. No GM gameplay eligibility exemption; normal authoring controls remain native.
- Glow through walls/floors is independent from actual tile artwork, which stays in native primary rendering and normal visibility/fog/level processing.
- Migrate legacy sensory definitions without removing unrelated Effect rules or creating duplicate world items. Existing Nakondis Particles is Item.ZLDzhzq0WaeeAreG: gold #ffd700, rank emission, hearing1, perception2/range30/wallsfalse.
- Native actor predicates use current canonical rules with the applied Effect as parent. Actorless tiles fail closed for predicate-dependent rules.
- Baseline sensory suite: 29/29 in 12 files. Keep unrelated movement work intact. Full suite runs serially because the unchanged clearance timing check is contention-sensitive.
- All subagents use gpt-6-astra. Primary personally reviews all changes. Keep existing local branch and small commits; no push/PR/merge is requested.

## Dependency-ordered slices

1. **Rule data and native registration.** Add the three rule source types, defaults/decoding, and schema-based native registration. Test mixed channels, omitted default fields, malformed/ignored rules, and actor-context evaluation. Inspect primary native source rather than inventing editor APIs.
2. **Shared resolution and consumers.** Resolve world rule arrays, keep application rank/provenance, and update emission/glow/hearing to consume independent rules. Test shared edits, deletion, multiple channels and per-rule range/threshold behavior without merging incompatible capabilities.
3. **Rules-tab configuration and migration.** Remove the Details editor; preserve shared-definition links beside native Rules. Migrate legacy world flags into system.rules without overwriting existing sensory/ordinary rules. Native copy identity applies to ordinary Effects needed by artwork conditions. Test migration idempotence and canonical-copy identity.
4. **Ambient broadcast channels.** Configure a direct channel string independently from Effect identity, preserving native sound fields and fail-closed private handling. Migrate legacy assignments safely; tests cover public/private clearing and same-file channel isolation.
5. **Conditional tile artwork.** Add Effect/minimum-rank tile controls and opacity gating with synchronous denial and native restoration. Test ANY selected-owned-PC behavior, expiry/deletion, removal, native refresh, unchanged masks/visibility/restrictions and absence of glow dependence. Wire existing lifecycle/init coverage.
6. **Delivery and manual acceptance.** Typecheck, lint, focused/full tests, build, diff review and an independent final review. Back up/sync the approved server build, preserving root manifest. Migrate/reuse Nakondis Particles. Document concise GM/player manual checks; do not run or wait for player-browser acceptance.

Each executable slice observes RED before GREEN and records actual checks. Split a slice again if its code/tests exceed 400 changed lines. Documentation changes do not need synthetic tests.

## Review focus

- Native forms remove default-valued fields; rule decoding must not silently disable saved rules.
- Shared world edits must reach existing applications without using stale embedded predicates or settings.
- Tile artwork denial must not remove tile depth/light/weather restrictions or clipping, and a later native refresh must not reveal denied artwork.
- Removing a condition restores current native opacity rather than an old cached value.
- Broken legacy audio references must stay private and silent; migration must not activate ordinary audio.

## Primary API evidence

Local PF2e source: src/scripts/set-game-pf2e.ts, src/module/rules/index.ts, src/module/item/base/sheet/rule-element-form/base.ts. The public registry is game.pf2e.RuleElements.custom; autogenForms uses native schema fields. Canonical rules are reconstructed with the applied Effect as parent before native predicate evaluation.

Foundry14.368 core reference: Tile._refreshMesh sets unoccludedAlpha/occludedAlpha; its color shader consumes both. The depth shader does not. refreshTile occurs after native render flags. Native mesh visibility and level filtering remain untouched. Public API: https://foundryvtt.com/api/classes/foundry.canvas.placeables.Tile.html

## Execution evidence

- Slices 1–5 implemented in focused commits. Behavioral RED/GREEN covered rule defaults,
  canonical edits, native Forms assignment, safe migration, and immediate tile denial.
- Full serial suite: 706 tests in 65 files passed before the final migration regression;
  all 64 sensory tests/18 files passed after review fixes.
- All three typechecks and both builds passed; lint has only the existing gridless
  `clearance` warning. No movement changes or relaxed assertions.
- Independent GPT-6 Astra review found two native-boundary issues: duplicate named
  controls in FormDataExtended and loss of disabled legacy definitions' broadcast
  channels during migration. Both were reproduced, fixed, and reviewed closed.
- Primary personally read production changes. Build deployed at `0ebcd97`; local and remote hashes match. GM reloaded; manual player acceptance remains user-owned.
